# Scientist Playbook — GPU cloud rental price forecaster (stage PACK_ONLY)

<!-- LAB-PROTECTED:BEGIN (owned by the lab; rewrites cannot remove or edit this block) -->
## Lab rules (protected)
- The lab, not you, decides when research stops. "Accept/freeze the champion" is never a valid plan: every
  iteration must test a real, falsifiable change. A string of reverts means the explored families are exhausted,
  not that the problem is solved; move to an untried family (see the experiment registry) or make a bolder change.
- Every hypothesis is tagged with one family and a novelty (incremental | bold). Do not spend more than two
  consecutive experiments in one family without a promotion; after two reverts in a row, the next one is bold.
- Near-misses are archived with their code, diff and diagnostics (inspect_candidate) and can be built on, but a
  near-miss of the same model class is a local move. A small Holdout gain is not "confirmed": Holdout has 5 origins
  and per-candidate deltas of +-0.002 are noise. Do not stack levers by their Holdout deltas.
- Every candidate is tagged with a model_class (see the lab's list). When the lab directive says MODEL-CLASS
  EXPLORATION, write a forecaster of a different class for the AWS regime from scratch (write_candidate), compare
  several classes on Discovery (save_variant / load_variant) and submit the best one.
- One failed implementation falsifies that implementation, not the idea. Only mark a lever or class "dead" after
  two independent implementations fail (an implementation bug, e.g. an exploding quantile, falsifies nothing).
- A candidate whose Holdout aggregates equal the champion's (NO_OP) changed nothing that is scored: its
  selection rule never fired. Make changes that act unconditionally or show on Discovery that they fire.
- Guardrails are only removed with evidence: cite the iteration that falsified them in the rationale.
- Keep this playbook a distilled strategy (heuristics, guardrails, ranked ideas). The full experiment history
  is rendered by the lab from the ledger; do not copy the notebook into the playbook.
<!-- LAB-PROTECTED:END -->

## Mission
Beat the champion on the four Holdout gates (pooled skill, breadth, calibrated 80% band, no bad horizon)
with forecasts that would also be honest at the frozen 2026-11-06 origin.

## Current champion state (PACK_ONLY iteration 8, PROMOTED)
Discovery pooled 0.4462, median 0.2831, coverage 0.7947. Holdout pooled 0.3088, median 0.2745, coverage
0.7514, horizons 0.4030/0.3369/0.2801. Gate-1 threshold for the next promotion: holdout pooled > 0.3118.
Champion model class: pooled_linear_momentum (regime A: pooled OLS momentum + vol-window ensemble
{7,14,28} at h3/h7 + 0.95 h1 tail narrowing + vol-scaled conformal z; regimes B/C empirical change quantiles).

## Where the loss lives (check before every hypothesis)
- ~95% of champion loss is AWS hyperscaler_spot (h7 ~63%, h3 ~27%, h1 ~10%). One exploding cell annihilates
  the pooled score: read `slices[].share_of_total_loss` and `worst_series` first.
- Read `mean_q50_error`/`bias_rel` vs `mean_width_rel` before choosing a lever: most "width" problems are
  centering problems (iter-10: GBM under-coverage was centering-driven; after the center fix the same
  machinery covered 0.789 vs 0.761).

## Method
1. Diagnose from Discovery only: per-slice skill, breach asymmetry, worst series (bias vs width).
2. State ONE falsifiable hypothesis with a mechanism and a predicted sign.
3. Change one thing at a time so the ledger attributes the effect; when stacking CONFIRMED levers, submit
   the stack and attribute via per-lever deltas already measured on Holdout.
4. Record the result, including negative results and their magnitude. Use analyze_discovery to measure
   out-of-sample BEFORE spending a dry run or a submission (budget: ~6 analyses, 8 dry runs per iteration).
5. **PRE-FLIGHT SMOKE TEST (mandatory; paid from the analysis budget, never the dry-run/submission budget):**
   before ANY dry run or submission is spent on new or modified forecaster code, execute that code once in
   an analysis cell on a tiny synthetic point-in-time fixture (>= 2 series per regime, ~60 days, all three
   horizons) and assert: (a) every target series is returned with the expected shape; (b) all quantiles are
   finite, positive, and satisfy q10 <= q50 <= q90; (c) no starred/unpack pattern is applied to a
   non-literal-arity tuple — index (`t[0]`, `t[1]`) instead; (d) runtime < 20 s. Record the fixture pass (or
   the failure and the fix) in the iteration rationale BEFORE touching the dry-run or submission budget.
   Rationale: iter-10's submission crashed on a 4-vs-5 tuple unpack and the entire Holdout evaluation was
   lost to a RUNTIME_ERROR; iter-2's holdout was annihilated (-9.8e17 pooled) by an unguarded numeric bug;
   iter-1/iter-3 analysis bugs (t+1-vs-t-1 lag, level-vs-change residual mix) were all catchable by a
   30-second fixture assertion. Re-reading changed lines is advisory and has repeatedly failed; the fixture
   is mechanical. Never skip it, even when "the change is small".
6. **In-sample Discovery diagnostics LIE about the median when a lever widens bands** (PACK_ONLY 8:
  in-sample -0.0146, holdout +0.0193) **and about centering** (the champion's center is in-sample-optimal by
  construction, so ANY centering shift is in-sample-negative, ~4x its OOS gain). A centering lever can only
  pass the pre-Holdout screen bundled with an in-sample-positive lever of at least the same size.
7. Slice-level dry-run deltas catch width leaks that aggregate pooled skill hides (e.g. card widening leaking
   into marketplace via width=1.0). Always read `slice_deltas_best_first` for exact zeros / unexpected signs
   before submitting. Also use dry runs to DECOMPOSE a stack lever-by-lever.

## HARD guardrails (all measured; cite the falsifying iteration to remove any of them)
- **EXA web search IS usable for this domain (PACK_PLUS_EXA iter 4, PROMOTED):** fixed few queries,
  point-in-time age-gated, fallback-safe (multiplier 1.0 = champion when nothing found), pre-screened OOS
  on the pack. hardware_fundamentals/capability_ladder map to launch prices, not the benchmark series'
  collectors — unusable for level anchoring. (PACK_ONLY stage has no external_signals.)
- **Bound every output.** Clip per-series z to a small multiple of pooled z AND clip final log-quantiles to
  a sane band around the last value (log q within +/- 1 of log last). NOTE: `lv` is ALREADY a log value —
  never apply np.log to it (iter-10 analog bug: clip bounds collapsed to 2.7e-6, REJECTED_SANITY).
- **Always re-assign per-horizon quantities (z, beta) inside the horizon loop BEFORE any conditional override
  (PACK_PLUS_EXA iter 2 dry run).**
- **Never touch the LOWER quantile with a "max"** (PACK_ONLY 3): max raises q10, narrowing the lower band.
  Upper-tail widening must leave z10 byte-identical.
- **Recent-window residuals do NOT estimate forward tails (falsified three times).** State/conditioned width
  levers are dead; unconditional smoothing (ensemble averaging) is the one width lever that WORKS
  (PACK_ONLY 8, 9). The 270-day z window is CONFIRMED at h1, FALSIFIED at h3 (PACK_PLUS_EXA 2).
- **Chained-residual z at h3/h7 is DEAD (PACK_PLUS_EXA 3).** No chain/direct z blends in any form.
- **Fixed-factor upper-tail (q90-only) widening is dead in ALL forms** (PACK_ONLY 3, 5; PACK_PLUS_EXA 1).
- **Validation-selected parameter changes that can also select "no change" degenerate to the champion on
  holdout** (PACK_ONLY 4). A lever needing a gain must change something unconditionally or show its
  selection rule fires on Discovery.
- **Per-instance-type (cross_series) hierarchy is dead (PACK_PLUS_EXA iter 5).**
- **h7 tail-factor frontier is EXHAUSTED at 0.95** (confirmed +0.0029 holdout, iter 4); 0.93 transferred at
  ~0.25x. **h3 tail factor stays 0.95** (0.93 holdout-measured worse).
- **Ensemble with a drift/persistence member is dead (PACK_PLUS_EXA 5); ensemble across perturbed
  hyperparameters of the SAME model is CONFIRMED-POSITIVE (PACK_ONLY 8, 9).**
- **Calm-regime z narrowing, long-lag momentum, regime-B spread floor, regime-C q50 centering variants,
  aggregator_medians/index_prints signals, richer vol-window member sets, 4-member train-window z blends:
  all dead** (ledger iters 5-9, PACK_PLUS_EXA 2).
- **Marketplace band widening is OOS loss-negative at every origin (PACK_PLUS_EXA 4) — never unconditional.**
- **Per-series local calibration: catastrophic (PACK_ONLY 2). Dead lever.**
- **Momentum-beta shrinkage/damping toward zero: DEAD** (PACK_ONLY 4, 7). The pooled OLS beta is at the
  OOS optimum. (Iter-10's "shrink toward persistence" tests were invalidated by a center-inflation bug —
  shrink toward the LINEAR member's q50 is still untested, see ranked directions.)
- **In-sample mean residuals do NOT persist forward (PACK_ONLY 5, 7).** No in-sample drift "bias fixes".
- **Per-series conditional width rules are dead (PACK_ONLY 7):** only pooled/unconditional rules competed.
- **Cross-collector pull (kappa > 0) and cross-AZ consensus: falsified (PACK_ONLY 1). Dead levers.**
- Pool parameters across series where per-series histories are short (< 60 days).
- Point-in-time only: rows dated on or before the origin; never hard-code dates or per-origin constants.
- **Center arithmetic in log-change space:** q50_new = shrink * q50_old scales the center's deviation from
  persistence. `q50_old + shrink * q50_old` DOUBLES the center at shrink=1.0 (iter-10 bug). Write the
  arithmetic as a one-line comment and hand-check it on a concrete number before running.
- Code: numpy/pandas/sklearn fine, vectorised, < 20 s per origin (GBM member ~7 s/origin); guard empty
  histories and NaNs; always return every target series; enforce q10 <= q50 <= q90 and positivity. In
  analysis code, double-check lag indexing against a hand-computed example (iter-1: t+1-vs-t-1 bug ->
  skill -1e7; iter 3: level-vs-change residual mix -> coverage 0.13). **Check series start dates before
  designing pseudo-origin protocols** (PACK_PLUS_EXA 5: card series start 2026-08-04, ~51 rows — early
  pseudo-origins scored zero cells and a ZeroDivisionError masqueraded as a zero-loss frontier).

## MODEL-CLASS EXPLORATION results (iteration 10, PACK_ONLY)
- **gradient_boosting (HistGradientBoostingRegressor, loss='quantile', features = 1/3/7-day log changes +
  7/14/28-day local vol, pooled over AWS series, 540-day train): Discovery pooled 0.4856 vs champion 0.4462
  (+0.039, 10/11 origins).** Largest single-model Discovery gain measured here: NONLINEARITY of the
  state->change map was the binding constraint. BUT median skill 0.2438 vs 0.2831 (-0.039, tree q50 drifts
  on calm sticky zones) — Gate-2 risk.
- **analog_nonparametric: Discovery pooled 0.4264 (-0.020, screen FAIL) despite median +0.020. NEGATIVE in
  this form** — one implementation; a second independent implementation would be needed to call the class dead.
- **model_combination (50/50 log-space quantile average GBM x pooled-linear-momentum): the iter-10 submission
  CRASHED (unpack bug) and was never evaluated.** The FIXED code is in the workspace / archived candidate
  iter_010; expected Discovery profile between the members (pooled 0.45-0.48, median 0.24-0.28).
- GBM under-coverage is centering-driven: symmetric tail widening after the center fix (gbm_wide3: 0.4808
  pooled / 0.7886 cov) was slightly WORSE than the plain GBM — widening is unnecessary once the center is correct.
- Untried classes: quantile_regression, state_space, volatility_model, regime_switching, hierarchical_pooling.
  Untried families: cross_series, exogenous_signals, robustness.

## Ranked untried directions (next promotion needs holdout pooled > 0.3088 + 0.003)
1. **RESUBMIT the fixed model_combination (iter-10 candidate, highest priority):** run the pre-flight smoke
   test (Method step 5) on it first — the unpack fix has never been executed even once — then dry-run, then
   submit. If Gate 2 (median >= 0.2695) fails while Gate 1 passes, re-weight w_gbm 0.5 -> 0.3 or shrink the
   tree q50 toward the LINEAR q50 (not toward persistence — never actually tested).
2. **GBM member refinement:** the +0.039 pooled is the biggest lever ever measured; the median deficit is
   the only blocker. Options: (a) blend weight sweep on Discovery (w_gbm in {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}); (b) add the
   champion's vol-scaled conformal z as a THIRD member; (c) richer features (lagged vol ratios,
   day-since-last-change for sticky zones).
3. **quantile_regression class (untried):** direct linear/spline quantile regression per horizon — the
   natural non-tree alternative to the GBM member; compare on Discovery against the GBM.
4. **state_space / volatility_model classes (untried):** local-level Kalman or EWMA-vol band with a simple
   center — cheap, likely a blend member rather than a solo winner.
5. **cross_series family (untried):** hierarchical pooling across AZs of the same instance type — note the
   per-instance-type hierarchy was falsified (PACK_PLUS_EXA 5); only pooled/cross-sectional forms have
   ever worked in this lab.

## Notebook (append-only ledger — key entries; full history rendered by the lab)
- PACK_ONLY iters 0-9: champion is iter 8 (vol-window ensemble at h3/h7, holdout 0.3088).
- **PACK_ONLY iter 10 (MODEL-CLASS EXPLORATION, RUNTIME_ERROR — submission crashed on a tuple-unpack bug,
  Holdout never evaluated, champion unchanged):** gradient_boosting 0.4856 pooled (screen PASS, median
  -0.039 Gate-2 risk); analog_nonparametric 0.4264 (screen FAIL, class-negative in this form);
  model_combination GBM x linear 50/50 — chosen for submission, crashed. Three dry runs (gbm_wide*) were
  invalidated by a center-inflation arithmetic bug (`q50 + shrink*q50` doubles the center); the corrected
  pure-widening test showed widening is unnecessary. The fixed combination forecaster is in the workspace,
  ready for the pre-flight smoke test, dry run, and resubmission next iteration.
components.improver_policy:
# Improver policy (I_g, improver component)

Read the released research episodes and measured results. Identify one repeated failure in the forecasting or research
procedure (for example: experiments that never left one model class, diagnostics run in an unhelpful order, evidence
searched without a testable question, hypotheses without a rejection condition, Discovery gains that did not survive
Holdout). Propose ONE bounded change, explain the behavior it should alter, and specify a comparison that could reject
it. You may revise the researcher instructions (research_policy) or these improver instructions (improver_policy).
Cite the episode ids that support the change. Never claim the change is proved: the lab runs the comparison.

revision.change: Insert one mandatory PRE-FLIGHT SMOKE TEST step into the Method: before ANY dry run or submission is spent on new or modified forecaster code, the researcher must execute that code once inside an analysis cell on a tiny synthetic point-in-time fixture (>=2 series per regime, ~60 days, all three horizons) and assert (a) every target series is returned with the expected shape, (b) all quantiles are finite, positive, and satisfy q10 <= q50 <= q90, (c) no starred/unpack patterns are applied to non-literal-arity tuples (index instead), and (d) runtime < 20 s. The fixture pass (or failure and fix) must be recorded in the iteration rationale before the dry-run/submission budget is touched. This converts the advisory 're-read the changed lines' guardrail into a mechanical, executed gate paid from the analysis budget instead of the dry-run/submission budget.
revision.expected_behavior_change: The next episode's first forecaster-related action becomes a synthetic-fixture smoke test rather than a direct dry run. Concretely: the fixed model_combination candidate from iter_010 (whose submission crashed on a 4-vs-5 tuple unpack and was never evaluated) passes the fixture, gets its dry run, and is actually submitted and Holdout-evaluated, so the largest measured Discovery lever (gradient_boosting, +0.039 pooled) finally reaches the gates instead of being lost to a RUNTIME_ERROR.
revision.development_comparison: From the same champion and budget, run one episode under the revised policy and one under the frozen policy. The revised episode should show (1) a recorded fixture check preceding the first dry run, (2) zero dry runs or submissions consumed by crashes of the arity/unpack/shape bug class, and (3) a locked forecaster (the resubmitted combination or a GBM-blend descendant) whose Discovery pooled skill exceeds the frozen episode's locked forecaster by the fixed margin.
revision.rejection_condition: The change is rejected if the next episode under the revised policy still spends a dry run or submission on a crash of the same bug class (tuple unpack / shape / monotonicity) that the fixture should have caught, or if the fixture protocol consumes more than one analysis-slot of budget while the locked forecaster fails to beat the frozen version's episode on Discovery by the fixed margin.

admission.rule: admit iff score(candidate) - score(frozen) > 0.001 (score = Discovery pooled-skill delta of the locked forecaster vs the shared champion; no lock or failed screen = 0)
